decision_tuple_contract.invalid_tuple_action: preserve received requested and supported, set active false, retain the incumbent path, and expose URING-FB-UNKNOWN
invariants: active implies requested is true, supported is SUPPORTED, and fallback_reason is URING-FB-NONE
unless fallback_reason is URING-FB-UNKNOWN, requested false implies supported is NOT_PROBED, active is false, and fallback_reason is URING-FB-NOT-REQUESTED
forced off implies supported is NOT_PROBED, active is false, and fallback_reason is URING-FB-FORCED-OFF
unless fallback_reason is URING-FB-UNKNOWN, supported UNSUPPORTED implies active is false and fallback_reason identifies the classified unsupported cause
a dependency-inactive capability is not probed, is inactive, and reports URING-FB-DEPENDENCY
any tuple violating these rules fails closed as inactive with URING-FB-UNKNOWN
URING-FB-UNKNOWN is the sole invariant exception: it preserves received requested and supported state while forcing active false

no_claims: The URING-2 checkpoint changes reactor selection, builder policy, driver observability metadata and bounded construction-time fixed-buffer, provided-group, multishot-accept, multishot-receive and requested-only SQPOLL probes; it changes no filesystem, TCP, bytes or advanced io_uring data-plane behavior.

Its RCH cargo checks prove default-feature and io-uring-feature library compilation only; the focused test attempt was stopped without a terminal test result and therefore proves no live-kernel outcome, capability activation or fallback behavior.
It does not prove buffer ownership, cancellation drain, descriptor cleanup or low-level boundary correctness.
It records no benchmark result and proves no latency, throughput, syscall, CPU, memory or efficiency improvement.
It does not prove broad workspace health, release readiness, production-on-by-default status or fleet availability.
It does not authorize dependency, capability or file removal, tracker closure, or any terminal ADOPT decision.
